findings.title: Single-cell batch reapplies every row
findings.why_it_matters: Applying even one staged correction now recomputes every row and output field before the corrected view appears. For the supported 10,000-row, 20-column workflow, correction latency therefore grows with the entire dataset rather than the number of touched rows, losing the prior incremental path and putting the documented 200 ms single-row target at risk. Evaluate the touched rows as one candidate batch, then publish the merged run only after all validation succeeds.
findings.suggested_fix: Generalize correctedRun's existing previous/changed-row path to accept the set of distinct edited row IDs: validate the candidate overlay, evaluate those rows, replace their results in the prior run, recount summary and csvRisk, and only then commit corrections/run/revision atomically. Fall back to full evaluation for a workflow change or workflow-level validation failure. Measure a 10,000-by-20 single-row correction as well as a multi-row batch.
